title: Dry Bulk Supply: Heavier Deliveries, but Ageing Fleet Offers a Buffer
section_path: Dry Bulk Supply: Heavier Deliveries, but Ageing Fleet Offers a Buffer
section_path_text: Dry Bulk Supply: Heavier Deliveries, but Ageing Fleet Offers a Buffer
summary:

Image reference: unsplash-image-j8urutZ8mc0.jpg | assets/2026-10-08_dry-bulk-supply-heavier-deliveries-but-ageing-fleet-offers-a-buffer_img_unsplash-image-j8urutz8mc0_d44eb921d781.jpg
By Eirini Diamantara & Dimitris Roumeliotis
Dry bulk supply growth has remained relatively manageable over the past three years, but the market is now moving into a more challenging phase as the orderbook expands and the delivery schedule becomes heavier. Across the Handysize, Supramax/Ultramax, Panamax/Kamsarmax and Capesize/Newcastlemax segments, the combined fleet has grown from approximately 972.4 mills DWT at the end of 2023 to around 1.066 bn DWT currently, an increase of about 9.6%. Annual fleet growth remained close to 3% in both 2024 and 2025 before accelerating modestly so far in 2026.
